scenarios.name: complete-statement-clean
scenarios.why: Typing a complete variable declaration statement into an empty function body resolves cleanly without syntax errors.

scenarios.name: incomplete-statement-syntax-error
scenarios.why: Stopping input before the terminating semicolon leaves an incomplete statement that triggers a syntax error.

scenarios.name: completed-statement-semicolon
scenarios.why: Completing the same variable declaration with a trailing semicolon resolves the pending syntax error.

scenarios.name: duplicate-variable-declaration
scenarios.why: Declaring an identifier that is already declared in the local function scope produces a duplicate symbol error.

scenarios.name: class-declaration-then-usage
scenarios.why: Declaring a class and subsequently declaring a variable of that class type ensures the type is recognized without unresolved-type errors.

scenarios.name: unresolved-type-variable
scenarios.why: Declaring a local variable with a type name that has never been declared must report an unresolved type diagnostic.

scenarios.name: missing-return-value
scenarios.why: Typing a bare return statement in a non-void function triggers a return-value-required diagnostic.

scenarios.name: completed-return-value
scenarios.why: Inserting a return value between return and semicolon clears the return-value-required error.

scenarios.name: function-body-line-by-line-return
scenarios.why: Progressively typing the statements of a non-void function line-by-line clears not-all-paths-return once the return statement is typed.

scenarios.name: class-body-method-declaration
scenarios.why: Adding a method declaration after an existing member field inside a class body parses and binds to the class cleanly.

scenarios.name: identifier-extending-prefix
scenarios.why: Typing a prefix that matches an existing identifier and then extending it into a longer existing identifier keeps references resolving without undeclared-identifier errors.

scenarios.name: multiline-block-variable-reference
scenarios.why: Typing multiple lines sequentially where subsequent lines reference variables declared in preceding lines resolves references without undeclared-identifier errors.
